asi.cache_semantics: key = relative path; value = (size, mtime_ns, result). Any write updates mtime so a stat match proves same content for all flows we control (event appends, receipts); shutil.copy2 preserves size+mtime so the staged copy reuses the source scan's per-file results; events.ndjson appended between scans only re-reads that one file. Stats taken AFTER read so fingerprint matches bytes actually read. Unreadable files never cached. Sensitive scan also populates the hash cache so the publishable digest after a scan hits per-file hashes instead of re-reading.
asi.hypothesis: per-file stat cache for _sensitive_candidates + _publishable_tree_digest: archive run scans same content 5x + digests 4x; cache per file instead of re-reading bytes each pass

description: sensitive-scan regex fast path: pre-lowered subject + case-sensitive patterns + literal keyword probe (14x faster matching, proven byte-equivalent)

asi.finding: root cause found via isolation: the scan's cost was NOT I/O but the (?i) regex - Python re cannot use its literal-prefix fast path under IGNORECASE and falls back to per-position alternation matching, 14x slower on binary data (measured: (?i) search 1.122s vs case-sensitive 0.080s over the same 600x24KB files). sha256 over the same data: 0.008s
asi.hypothesis: regex fast path for the sensitive scan: pre-lower subject bytes (bytes.lower(): ASCII-only, length-preserving, C speed) + strip (?i) from the patterns (all-lowercase ASCII literals) + two-stage probe (pure literal keyword alternation as necessary condition; full patterns only on probe hit). Byte-for-byte equivalent to (?i) on bytes patterns because bytes-mode case folding is ASCII-only and offsets are preserved
asi.micro_evidence: warm-tree scan: ~1.15s -> 0.242s serial (regex portion eliminated); benchmark gain ~0.13s because the scan pool already parallelizes the regex work across 8 workers over only the first pass's real reads. Defender first-read tax on fresh fixture files (up to 8.5ms/file) dominates the benchmark's cold reads and is environment, not code

New public helper harness_runtime.scanned_file_digest(path, relative): returns the scan-recorded hex digest after verifying (size, mtime_ns), None on any doubt (unscanned tree, scan policy off, evicted cache, file changed since scan). _parallel_copytree uses it before falling back to a real read. Relative-path keying sound within the tree lineage: the scan walked exactly the copy source (or a byte-identical copy2 copy)
asi.real_scale: gain scales linearly with change-tree size: 600 files -> 0.4s; a 3000-file tree -> ~2s per archive
asi.verification: three-path differential: (1) with prior scan 60/60 digests available, transfer-vs-disk 0 mismatches; (2) no scan (fresh caches) fallback real reads 0 mismatches; (3) file mutated after scan -> scanned_file_digest returns None (no stale digest), copied file gets the NEW correct hash. In-execute: scanned_file_digest reused 608 times (all copy source reads eliminated). 229 archive+runtime tests green; candidate B (render x7 on 800 events = 4ms/render) measured negligible and closed

description: archive append_event: render execution-log only on phase.end/auto-seal and respect render-policy (contract alignment + large-log churn fix; benchmark-neutral)

asi.bug_found: harness_archive.append_event violated the events §6.1 contract TWO ways: (1) it re-rendered the full execution-log after EVERY append (CLI path only renders on phase.end/auto-seal - 'normal appends are O(1)'); (2) it ignored render-policy.json (projects configuring executionLog=on-demand still got forced full re-renders). Fix aligns archive appends with the CLI contract: render only on phase.end/auto-seal AND respect render-policy. The archive terminal phase.end renders before collect/summary which consumes the log, so freshness dependency is preserved (verified by reading the finalize step order: freeze -> collect happens AFTER the terminal phase.end append)
asi.ab_test: back-to-back A/B: WITHOUT median 5.84, WITH median 5.81 - benchmark-neutral as expected (fixture log is a few KB). run_experiment median 5.06 (4.95/5.03/5.06/5.07/5.09)
asi.hypothesis: events append render churn on large logs: breakdown of the 0.368s/7-append cost on a 1.25MB log showed load 0.058 + render 0.041 + write 0.022 = 0.12s accounted, the rest was write-amplification on the 1.1MB rendered log per append (Defender). With the fix, only the terminal phase.end renders: 6 mechanical appends 0.142s + 1 phase.end 0.037s vs 7x full render before - on a 1.25MB log saves ~0.2s per archive; scales with log size

description: final stability confirmation (5.04s, -85.6%); hypothesis pool formally closed - last candidate (hardlink durable copy) rejected as benchmark overfit + durability violation

asi.hypothesis: final stability confirmation + hypothesis pool closure. Last candidate considered and REJECTED: hardlink-based durable copy (same-volume os.link would save the 1.7s copy in the benchmark) - rejected on both honesty and semantic grounds: (1) benchmark places the durable root on the same volume as the project, but the real contract requires durable root OUTSIDE the project (typically cross-volume) where hardlinks fail - the gain would be a benchmark artifact, textbook overfitting; (2) same-volume hardlinks would make the 'immutable' durable object share an inode with the archive directory - any later byte change to the archived tree would rewrite the durable object, breaking durability semantics
